sources.fact: Flood Zones dataset last updated 6 July 2026; Flood Zones 2 and 3 are supplied while Zone 1 is the remainder outside those extents.
Flood Zones plus climate change updated 6 July 2026 and provides OGC API Features, WFS/WMS and downloadable GeoPackage/GeoJSON/GDB resources.
Present-day surface-water extents use 0.1%, 1% and 3.3% AEP scenarios and are not suitable for individual-property risk conclusions.
Climate-change surface-water extents updated 6 July 2026 use UKCP18 RCP8.5 upper-end 2070s scenario for long-term planning.
Present-day surface-water depth data uses AEP scenarios and depth bands but remains area-level planning evidence.
Climate-change depth layers provide bands from up to 150mm through over 2300mm for the modelled AEP scenarios.
Official service supports planning flood-risk lookup, printable maps and ordering detailed flood-risk data.
Updated 28 May 2026; applicants must determine whether a site-specific FRA and sustainable drainage information are needed.
Climate-change allowances cover peak river flow, rainfall intensity, sea-level rise and other parameters and must be selected for the relevant assessment.
Updated 28 May 2026; LPA checks include site research, development class, FRA need, SuDS, sequential/exception tests and consultation routes.
Applicant standing advice updated 28 May 2026; it does not replace site-specific evidence where a full FRA is required.
Planning guidance requires sequential consideration of flood risk and recognises other flood sources beyond mapped river/sea zones.

examples.result: Flood-zone polygon intersection is retained as screening evidence, not a complete site-specific FRA.
Flood Zone 1 is not represented by fabricating a polygon; it is derived only under the official zone semantics.
Surface-water datasets explicitly unsuitable for individual-property risk are not converted into parcel probability scores.
Climate-change and present-day layers remain separate and are not mixed into one undocumented risk value.
Defence benefits are not inferred from Flood Zones because the mapped zones ignore defence benefits.
OGC/WFS/GeoJSON availability is an acquisition route, not proof that exact candidate overlay has been executed.
Sequential/exception-test need depends on site and proposal context, not just centroid zone lookup.
No flood promotion occurs until exact parcel overlay, current datasets and site-specific FRA/assessment evidence are bound where required.
